\tabnotes{The table replicates \citet{cieslak2015}, Table~1, on United States
  data, 1989m3--2014m12. Panel~A reports the maturity-by-maturity projection of
  yields on trend inflation,
  $y^{(n)}_{t}=a_{n}+b_{n}\,\tau^{\mathrm{CPI}}_{t}+\varepsilon^{(n)}_{t}$
  \eqref{eq:decomp}, where $\tau^{\mathrm{CPI}}_{t}$ is the discounted moving
  average of realised core CPI inflation \eqref{eq:trendinf}; intercepts are
  scaled by $100$ and expressed in basis points, and $t$-statistics are
  Newey--West adjusted ($18$ lags). Panel~B reports the standard deviation (in
  percent) and the AR(1) half-life (in months), computed as
  $\ln(0.5)/\ln(|\hat{\psi}|)$ for AR(1) coefficient $\hat{\psi}$, of the
  maturity-specific cycle $\cyc^{(n)}_{t}$ defined as the residual of
  \eqref{eq:decomp} and of the corresponding yield $y^{(n)}_{t}$. Because the
  sample is shorter than the 1975--2014 window of \citet{cieslak2015},
  intercept levels differ and the cycle half-lives are shorter; the slopes and
  $\bar{R}^{2}$ align with the original.}
